subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Unit 4: Civilisation – Project: An Archaeological Site in Oman
outcomes: Choose reliable sources and check facts.
Make a clear leaflet with my team and review others' work.

tf.s: An archaeological site is a place where evidence of the past is found.
Al Baleed Archaeological Park is an archaeological site in Oman.
tf.why: Correct, it was one of the sites in the lesson.

tf.s: A leaflet gives short information about a place.
tf.why: Right, leaflets are short and clear.

tf.s: A travel blog is always a reliable source.
tf.why: Not always; we must check the source.

tf.s: A reliable source is accurate and trustworthy.
tf.why: Well done, we can trust its information.

tf.s: 'The fort were built in the 17th century.' is correct.
tf.why: 'The fort' is singular, so we say 'was built'.

tf.s: 'When was it built?' is a good research question about a site.
tf.why: Yes, it asks for a key fact.

tf.s: Teamwork means everyone works alone without sharing.
tf.why: Teamwork means sharing roles and working together.

tf.s: A leaflet about a site can include its name, location, history and importance.
tf.why: Correct, these are the key details.

tf.s: When we review another team's leaflet, we should only say bad things.
tf.why: Good reviews include strengths and polite suggestions.

boxes.q: Where is evidence of the past found?
boxes.why: These sites hold clues about the past.

boxes.q: A ___ gives short information about a place.
The fort ___ built in the 17th century.
Is a travel blog always reliable?
o: Not always; we must check it.

boxes.q: Which is a good research question?
boxes.why: It asks about the site's history.

boxes.q: Which is an archaeological site in Oman?
Something that is true and can be checked is a…

hunt.q: Place with evidence of the past

o: a place where evidence of the past is found
a place where new cars are sold
mcq.why: These sites show how people lived long ago.

mcq.q: Which is an archaeological site in Oman named in the lesson?
mcq.why: Bibi Miriam's Shrine was one of the Omani sites.

mcq.q: What information goes in the leaflet?
o: the site's name, location, history and importance
mcq.why: These details tell readers about the site.

mcq.q: Complete: The fort ___ in the 17th century.
Your team is researching a site. Which pair of research questions is best?
o: When was it built? Who discovered it?
Do you like pizza? Are you tired?
What time is it? Where is my bag?
Is it raining? Who is your teacher?
mcq.why: Good questions ask about the site's history.

mcq.q: Which comment is a helpful review of another team's leaflet?
o: The design is clear, but you could add the site's location.
mcq.why: Give a strength and a suggestion.

mcq.q: Why must you check the sources you use?
o: To make sure the information is correct.

mcq.q: Which source is most likely to be reliable for facts about a site?
o: an official website about the site
a funny video with no source
mcq.why: Official sources are usually checked and accurate.

mcq.q: Why is it useful to reflect on your teamwork after the project?
o: It helps you find what to improve next time.
It means you do not need to work.
It is only for the teacher.
